title: Lifting a cocone through a right fibration is a path in its section space
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, quasicategories, spaces, coherent transformations and cocones of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], right fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and transport and classifiers of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification]. Fix a universe of small simplicial sets. Let $q:I\to A$ be a right fibration of small quasicategories, classified by $X:A^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S$. Let $K$ be any small simplicial set, $p:K\to A$ a diagram, and $t:K\to I$ a lift with $qt=p$. Write $\Gamma_p=\operatorname{Fun}_{/K}(K,K\times_A I)$ for the Kan space of sections: its $n$-simplices are maps $K\times\Delta^n\to I$ over $p\operatorname{pr}_K$. The classification mapping-space formula identifies $\Gamma_p$ with $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)}(\Delta *,Xp^{\mathrm{op}})$, and $t$ determines a point $s_t$ of this space.

Let $b\in A$, let $\lambda:p\to\Delta_Kb$ be a coherent cocone, represented by $K\times\Delta^1\to A$, and let $x\in I_b$, regarded as a point of $X(b)$ via the classifier. The composite $\Delta *\xrightarrow{x}\Delta X(b)\xrightarrow{X\lambda}Xp^{\mathrm{op}}$ determines a point $s_{\lambda,x}\in\Gamma_p$, up to the coherent identifications just specified. Define the space of lifted cocones over $\lambda$ to be the homotopy fiber over $\lambda$ of
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,I)}(t,\Delta_Kx)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,A)}(p,\Delta_Kb).$$
This space is naturally equivalent to the path space from $s_t$ to $s_{\lambda,x}$ in $\Gamma_p$. Moreover, a point of this homotopy fiber can be represented by an actual coherent transformation $t\to\Delta_Kx$ whose image under $q$ is the prescribed cylinder $\lambda$. Thus a path between the two section points supplies a coherent cocone in $I$ over $\lambda$, with apex $x$. The equivalence and this realization retain simplicial parameters and are natural under restriction of $K$. The shape $K$ need not be a quasicategory, and $K=\varnothing$ is allowed.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.5.4, printed p.404: agent-expanded coherent lifting calculation in the right-fibration/category-of-elements proof; uses the transport mapping-space formula of Section 2.2. This auxiliary statement is not quoted verbatim from HTT. Online source not archived in literature/.

proof.text:
For a small simplicial set $Z$ and $a:Z\to A$, write $\Gamma_a$ for the simplicial set of maps $Z\times\Delta^n\to I$ over $a$. The pullback $Z\times_A I\to Z$ is a right fibration: project a horn lifting square to $I\to A$ and pair its filler with the prescribed simplex of $Z$. By the constant-functor and pullback clauses of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification], the identity right fibration $Z\to Z$ classifies $\Delta *$, the pullback classifies $Xa^{\mathrm{op}}$, and the mapping-space formula gives
$$\Gamma_a\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(Z^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)}(\Delta *,Xa^{\mathrm{op}}).$$
In particular $\Gamma_a$ is Kan. This holds for arbitrary simplicial $Z$. At $Z=K$ the section $t$ is precisely the stated point $s_t$.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.3.11, contravariant mapping-space and pullback comparison; setup for the auxiliary lifting calculation below Corollary 5.3.5.4.

proof.text:
We need restriction on strict sections, not only its effect on components. Let $J\subseteq Z$ be a simplicial subset and fix $a:Z\to A$. Restriction $\Gamma_a\to\Gamma_{a|_J}$ is a right fibration. Indeed a lifting square for $\Lambda_i^n\subseteq\Delta^n$, $0<i\leq n$, transposes to the lifting square for $q$ with domain
$$(Z\times\Lambda_i^n)\cup_{J\times\Lambda_i^n}(J\times\Delta^n)\ \subseteq\ Z\times\Delta^n.$$
This is right anodyne by [lem-coef-infinity-right-anodyne-product], applied to the right horn and $J\subseteq Z$, after interchanging factors. The trivial-Kan exponential corner of [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-exponentiation] supplies the lift of this square. By Step 1 the target section space is Kan, so [lem-cbc-right-fibration-space-fiber] makes restriction a Kan fibration. This argument also applies after fixing any compatible section on $J$ by pullback.

source.place: Corollaries 2.1.2.7 and 2.1.2.9, right-handed forms; explicit adjunction of each horn problem.

proof.text:
Put $C=K\times\Delta^1$, with its prescribed map $\lambda:C\to A$, and set
$$T=\{H:C\to I\text{ over }\lambda\mid H|_{K\times\{1\}}=\Delta_Kx\},$$
where degree $n$ means maps $C\times\Delta^n$ with this endpoint condition throughout the parameter. The inclusion $K\times\{1\}\subseteq C$ is right anodyne: it is the pushout-product of $\{1\}=\Lambda_1^1\subseteq\Delta^1$ and $\varnothing\subseteq K$, by [lem-coef-infinity-right-anodyne-product]. Pull back the trivial Kan fibration of [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-exponentiation] over the fixed pair $(\lambda,\Delta_Kx)$. It gives $T\to *$ a trivial Kan fibration. Boundary lifting is preserved by this pullback. By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], $T$ is a nonempty contractible Kan complex. Choose $H_0\in T$ and write $u=H_0|_{K\times\{0\}}$. The initial restriction $r:T\to\Gamma_p$ is a Kan fibration: apply Step 2 to $K\times\partial\Delta^1\subseteq C$, and then pull back along the subspace of endpoint sections with final section $\Delta_Kx$.

source.place: Corollaries 2.1.2.7, 2.1.2.9 and 2.1.2.10, right-handed forms, with fixed final section.

proof.text:
Identify $u$ under Step 1. Pullback compatibility in [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] identifies the classifier over $C$ with $F=X\lambda^{\mathrm{op}}$. Currying in the interval direction regards $F$ as the edge
$$X\lambda:\Delta_K X(b)\longrightarrow Xp^{\mathrm{op}}$$
in $\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$; the interval is reversed because $X$ is contravariant. The section $H_0$ corresponds to a coherent transformation $\Delta *\to F$. Its restrictions at the two ends are respectively $u$ and the constant point $x$. The naturality data of this transformation along the reversed interval identify its value $u$ with the composite $(X\lambda)\circ\Delta x$. This identification is on the mapping spaces, with their homotopies: the classification comparison preserves composition and pullbacks, not merely vertex fibers. Thus $u$ represents exactly $s_{\lambda,x}$ under the coherent identifications allowed in the statement. All choices here may be retained as the contractible space $T$, rather than selecting unrelated endpoint identifications.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.3.11, composition and pullback compatibility; explicit endpoint calculation for the cylinder, not a quotation from Corollary 5.3.5.4.

proof.text: We compare the stated homotopy fiber with strict cylinders. Put $D=\operatorname{Fun}(K,I)$, $B=\operatorname{Fun}(K,A)$, and $Q=\operatorname{Fun}(K,q)$. They are quasicategories by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. The map $Q$ is an inner fibration: an inner-horn lifting problem transposes to $K\times\Lambda_i^n\subseteq K\times\Delta^n$, which is inner anodyne by [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product] with $\varnothing\subseteq K$, and $q$ lifts it. Write $U_D(t,\Delta_Kx)$ and $U_B(p,\Delta_Kb)$ for fixed-endpoint arrow spaces. By [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation] their map induced by $Q$ is a Kan fibration. The natural pinch equivalences of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] give a commutative square from the right-pinched mapping-space map in the item to this arrow-space map, with both horizontal maps weak equivalences. [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection], with the lower map the pinch equivalence, identifies their homotopy fibers over $\lambda$. On vertices the pinch sends an edge to that same edge, so this is the prescribed cylinder $\lambda$. Finally [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison] identifies the latter homotopy fiber with its strict fiber. By currying, that strict fiber is exactly $L=r^{-1}(t)$: its simplices are cylinders over $\lambda$ with initial section $t$ and final section $\Delta_Kx$.

source.place: Proposition 1.2.7.3, Corollary 2.3.2.4 and the natural arrow/right-pinched mapping-space comparison; explicit strict-fiber comparison.

proof.text:
Now use the contractibility of $T$, rather than discarding its higher simplices. Form the path pullback $P(t,r)$ of $\{t\}\to\Gamma_p\leftarrow T$: a simplex consists of $H\in T$ and a path from $t$ to $r(H)$. Since $r$ is a Kan fibration, [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison] gives a weak equivalence $L\to P(t,r)$ by the constant path. The inclusion $\{H_0\}\to T$ is a weak equivalence because $T\to *$ is one and their composite is the identity of $*$. Apply [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] to the maps of cospans with components $1_{\{t\}}$, $1_{\Gamma_p}$ and $\{H_0\}\hookrightarrow T$. It gives a weak equivalence
$$\operatorname{Path}_{\Gamma_p}(t,u)=P(t,u)\longrightarrow P(t,r).$$
Here paths go from $t$ to $u$, in the required direction. Hence $L\simeq\operatorname{Path}_{\Gamma_p}(s_t,s_{\lambda,x})$ by Step 4. Together with Step 5 this proves the claimed equivalence of spaces, including cases where both sides are empty.

source.place: Agent-written path-pullback calculation of the fixed-initial-endpoint fiber; Kan homotopy pullback comparison.

proof.text: There is also an actual lift over the prescribed cylinder. Given a path $\alpha:\Delta^1\to\Gamma_p$ from $t$ to $u$, use the right-fibration lifting property of $r$ (Step 2) on $\{1\}=\Lambda_1^1\subseteq\Delta^1$ with target $H_0$. Its lift $\widetilde\alpha$ has $r(\widetilde\alpha(0))=t$. The vertex $H=\widetilde\alpha(0)\in T$ is an actual map $K\times\Delta^1\to I$ with $qH=\lambda$, initial section $t$ and final section $\Delta_Kx$. Thus it is a coherent cocone with apex $x$, with exact prescribed image. More generally Step 5 shows that every point of the original homotopy fiber is represented up to its homotopy-fiber identification by such an $H$: the strict-fiber comparison is an equivalence of Kan spaces, so every component has a strict representative. This assertion does not identify arbitrary chosen simplicial models of the homotopy fiber literally with the strict fiber.

source.place: Corollary 2.1.2.10, right-handed endpoint lifting; actual representative, not only existence of a path class.

proof.text: All the comparisons before choosing $H_0$ are restriction, pullback, currying, pinch, or constant-path maps. They commute with restriction along every $K'\to K$: on a parameter simplex the map is precomposition with $K'\times\Delta^1\times\Delta^n\to K\times\Delta^1\times\Delta^n$. The choice-free intermediate cospan in Step 6 uses $T$ itself. Choosing $H_0$ only replaces its contractible end by a point; the contractible Kan space $T$ supplies paths between choices and their higher compatibility data, and applying $r$ supplies exactly the endpoint comparisons. Thus the resulting equivalence is natural as an equivalence of spaces under restriction, with simplicial parameters retained. Step 7 has relative parameters too: the right-anodyne pushout-product with a parameter boundary and the exponential corner of [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-exponentiation] extend prescribed compatible target-lift data. No step uses a horn filler in $K$ or assumes $K$ nonempty. If $K=\varnothing$, all functor, section, cylinder and mapping spaces here are points. For constant $q:I\to *$ with $I$ Kan, the calculation reduces to the usual paths in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,I)$; unequal components give empty lift and path spaces.

source.place: Corollaries 2.1.2.7 and 2.1.2.9 with parameter boundaries; naturality of Proposition 2.2.3.11 and the explicit cylinder construction.
